competency: M1 stated values with instrument record fields, uncertainty and conditions (as known at a mark)
question: As known at mark before-t4, which temperature values of kiln-k3 hold at T5 12:00, and for measurement t1 what SI range, raw value, raw unit, standard uncertainty, coverage factor, conditions and calibration reference were recorded, and is t1 accepted? Is lab-veld's t3 usable for the system?
justification: measurements lists one entry per visible has-quality attestation about (kiln-k3, temperature) (ME §2); with t = T5h12, SD-MEA-1 includes every attestation whose verdict at t is not silent: t1 [T3,T6), t2 [T4,T7), t3 [T5,T7) and the statement s1 [T4,T8); t4 is recorded after before-t4 and is invisible (common 0.2). t1's range is [v - k u, v + k u] converted to SI with SI = value x 1 + 273.15 (ME §2 range; calc sheet). Record fields are as written (D-C-1, D-C-7; conditions as exact text). The system accepts its own claims, so t1 is accepted and usable (usable = accepted, not superseded, supporting stance, polarity true). t3 is lab-veld's claim, which nobody in the system perspective accepted: unreviewed, so not usable. Evidence: usable measurement entries t1 and t2 are supporting (P-ME-1); s1 is a usable statement and this is a 'values stated' question, so it is admissible but not required; t3 is an alternative (v0.2 §6.2) and t4 is invisible at as_of, so both are forbidden.
uncertainty: raw_unit is expected as the unit id the fixture wrote ('as written'); conditions are compared as written.

competency: M1 stated value with uncertainty and instrument (two readers: measurements then measurement_calibration)
question: As known at before-t4, what value, standard uncertainty, coverage factor and SI range did measurement t2 of kiln-k3's temperature report at T5 12:00, and with which instrument was it taken?
justification: s1: t2 is visible at before-t4 and holds at T5h12 ([T4,T7)); its record keeps raw value 452.6, u = 0.5 and k = 2 as written (ME §2, D-C-1); its range is [452.6 - 1.0, 452.6 + 1.0] degC = [724.75, 726.75] K (calc sheet). s2: measurement_calibration gives one row per (record, activity instrument) and reports the activity's instrument (MC §2), which the measure step names as therm-b. Evidence: t2 is a usable measurement (supporting, P-ME-1 / P-MC-1). The full answers also contain t1 (usable), the statement s1 and the established calibration claims cal-ta and cal-tb cited in each row's attested.support (MC §6 'C-4 inherited'), so those are admissible. t3 (unreviewed) is an alternative and t4 is invisible at the mark: forbidden.

competency: M1 a stated (not measured) value in a non-SI unit, as listed by measurements (slot T-M6)
question: As known at before-t4, which values of kiln-k3's temperature have been stated at T5 12:00? In particular, how is the plain statement s1 (840 to 850 degF, no measurement record) listed: as a measurement or a statement, accepted or not, usable or not, and with which records?
justification: s1 is an attest of has-quality(kiln-k3, temperature, unit degF) with lower/upper parameters and no measurement record. ME §2: kind is 'measurement' when the entry rests on records and 'statement' when it has none (stage-c C0 'stay separate'), so s1 is a statement with no records. The system wrote it and accepts its own claims: accepted; polarity true, supporting stance, not superseded: usable. It holds at T5h12 ([T4,T8)) and is visible at the mark. Evidence: the ME evidence table makes a usable statement supporting for a 'values stated' question, which this is, so s1 is required; the usable measurements t1 and t2 are also listed and admissible. t3 (unreviewed) is an alternative and t4 is invisible: forbidden. The statement's range is deliberately not expected: the contracts do not fix whether a statement written in a non-SI unit is reported in SI (see ambiguities.md A-3).
spec: stage-c C0 via contracts compare_measurements §2 (statements listed apart)
uncertainty: The ME evidence row for statements is labelled 'supporting or alternative' for a 'values stated' question; this gold reads it as supporting because the question asks which values have been stated. records = [] reads 'statement (no record)' as an empty records list.

competency: M1 stated values judged from another perspective (lab-veld)
question: From lab-veld's perspective, as known at before-t4, which of the temperature values of kiln-k3 that hold at T5 12:00 are accepted and usable?
justification: Acceptance is judged per perspective (ME §3; v0.2 §6.2): lab-veld's perspective is its own attestations (t3) plus what it accepted (t1, by the accept step before the mark). t2 and s1 are the system's claims, which lab-veld never accepted: unreviewed, hence not usable. All four are visible at before-t4 and hold at T5h12 (SD-MEA-1); t4 is recorded after the mark. Nothing is merged across perspectives (common 0.2). Evidence: usable measurement entries t1 and t3 support (P-ME-1); t2 and s1 are alternatives for lab-veld; t4 is invisible.

competency: M2 agreement asked at a knowledge time before any measurement was recorded
question: As known at mark start (before any temperature value was recorded), do the temperature measurements of kiln-k3 at T5 12:00 agree?
justification: At @start no has-quality attestation about (kiln-k3, temperature) has been recorded; t1 to t4 and s1 are all written after the mark and are invisible (common 0.2; one measurement is visible all together or not at all, D-C-8). CM §3: with no comparable incompatible pair and no compared measurements, the status is UNKNOWN when something is held and NOT_YET_KNOWN when nothing is; §0.3: NOT_YET_KNOWN means nothing relevant is recorded or visible at as_of. With nothing compared there are no pairs. Nothing can be cited.

competency: M2 agreement within uncertainty from another perspective (disjoint ranges: incompatible)
question: From lab-veld's perspective, as known at before-t4, do the kiln-k3 temperature measurements at T5 12:00 agree within their stated uncertainties?
justification: CM compares the measurements the perspective accepts (CM §1, §4). For lab-veld these are t3 (its own) and t1 (accepted by lab-veld); t2 is unreviewed for lab-veld and t4 is invisible at the mark. t1 = [723.55, 725.15] K and t3 = [730.15, 732.15] K: same coverage (k = 2), same condition texts, same SI unit and overlapping valid times at T5h12, so comparable; closed-bound overlap fails (725.15 < 730.15), so the pair is incompatible and the status is DISPUTED (CM §3; v0.2 clarification B). Evidence: CM §6 makes the members of an incompatible pair conflicting and excludes them from supporting, so t1 and t3 are required conflicting evidence and nothing is supporting. t2 and s1 are alternatives for lab-veld; t4 is invisible.

competency: M2 agreement within uncertainty with three measurements, after a later recording (latest knowledge)
question: With everything recorded (no as_of), do the system's temperature measurements of kiln-k3 at T5 12:00 agree, and how are the statement and lab-veld's measurement treated?
justification: System-usable measurements holding at T5h12: t1 [723.55, 725.15], t2 [724.75, 726.75], t4 [739, 741] K (t4 is visible with no as_of). All have k = 2 and identical condition texts. Pairs (one per pair, CM §5): t1-t2 overlap (724.75 <= 725.15 and 723.55 <= 726.75): possibly compatible; t1-t4 and t2-t4 disjoint: incompatible. Any comparable incompatible pair makes the status DISPUTED (CM §3). s1 has no result record, so it is listed under statements, never compared (stage-c C0); t3 is unaccepted by the system and is listed in alternatives (CM §2). Evidence (CM §6): every compared measurement is in an incompatible pair, so none is supporting; t1, t2, t4 are conflicting. Statements and alternatives are never cited. Contrast with M-001's mark before-t4, where t4 was invisible.

competency: M2 agreement asked from a perspective that has accepted nothing
question: From operator op-rhee's perspective (op-rhee has made and accepted no claims), as known at before-t4, do the temperature measurements of kiln-k3 at T5 12:00 agree?
justification: op-rhee is only the operator named in the activities; it attested nothing and accepted nothing, so every visible claim (t1, t2, t3, s1) is unreviewed for op-rhee and nothing is compared (CM §1 'compares the measurements the perspective accepts'; v0.2 §6.2; nothing is merged across perspectives, common 0.2). With no compared measurement there are no pairs and no core-rule status; records about the quality are visible, so the status is UNKNOWN, not NOT_YET_KNOWN (CM §3; §0.3 'UNKNOWN: something relevant is recorded, but no answer follows'; v0.2 §5.6). Unaccepted claims are alternatives and never cited.
uncertainty: CM §3 says 'UNKNOWN when something is held'; this gold reads 'held' as 'recorded and visible', in line with §0.3 and v0.2 §5.6.

competency: M6 calibration at measurement time, with stated reference checked against certificates
question: As known at before-t4, were the instruments that took t1 and t2 calibrated when those measurements were taken, and does each measurement's stated calibration reference match a certificate?

expected.[attestation=t2].reference_check.check: no certificate with the stated reference

justification: t selects the measurements (SD-MEA-1): t1, t2, t3 hold at T5h12 (s1 is a statement: no rows). Calibration is judged at each activity's start (MC §4; D-D3-2): t1 starts T3, inside cal-ta's [T1, T20); t2 starts T4, inside cal-tb's [T1, until superseded). Each is the only, accepted holding: rule Q gives established, status by the core rule over the system's (non-stipulated, non-inferred) claim: ASSERTED (CS §3), support the deciding claim (C-4). Reference checks (MC §2, d3 §3): t1 states 'CAL-TA-2026-01', the exact reference of cert-ta, a certificate naming therm-a: matches a certificate. t2 states 'CAL-TB-77' while therm-b's only certificate has reference 'CAL-TB-78': exact text differs (G-6), so no certificate with the stated reference. The two are reported side by side and never reconciled: the mismatch does not change the attested judgement (MC §3). Evidence: usable rows t1, t2 and the established support cal-ta, cal-tb (MC §6). t3 is unreviewed (alternative); t4 invisible.
uncertainty: attested.status ASSERTED assumes the system's calibrate claims have a non-stipulation, non-inference basis (the fixture format gives none other).

competency: M5 affine conversion (degC to kelvin)
question: What is 20 degC in kelvin?
justification: CV §3: a unit owns dimension, si-factor and si-offset; SI = value x si_factor + si_offset, and the value in the target unit is (SI - offset_to) / factor_to. degC (factor 1, offset 273.15) and kelvin (factor 1, offset 0) are both temperature. 20 x 1 + 273.15 = 293.15 K. No status, no evidence (CV §2, §6); no derivation (CV §7).
uncertainty: convert takes no world (CV §1), so the step has no world parameter; 'value' names the bare float answer.

competency: M5 affine-to-affine conversion (degF to degC)
question: What is 98.6 degF in degC?
justification: Both units are temperature (CV §1). SI = 98.6 x 0.5555555555555556 + 255.3722222222222 = 310.15 K; in degC: (310.15 - 273.15) / 1 = 37.0 (calc sheet; floating-point residue about 6e-14, inside the tolerance). No status or evidence (CV §2, §6).
uncertainty: convert takes no world; 'value' names the bare float answer.

competency: M5 scale conversion (gram to kilogram)
question: What is 1,500 g in kilograms?
justification: gram (factor 0.001, offset 0) and kilogram (factor 1, offset 0) are both mass. SI = 1500 x 0.001 = 1.5 kg; in kilogram (1.5 - 0) / 1 = 1.5 (CV §3; E2 M5).
uncertainty: convert takes no world; 'value' names the bare float answer.

competency: M5 conversion across dimensions (established refusal)
question: What is 1,500 g in degC?
justification: CV §1: 'to' must be a unit of the same dimension; CV §8 lists the cross-dimension refusal (ValueError 'cannot convert ...') as established [E] (stage-c C1 API). gram is mass, degC is temperature, and both units are defined in the fixture, so this is the documented refusal, not a precondition failure (common 0.8).

competency: M1 a measured value recorded against an alias of the bearer, asked by the canonical name through facts_about (slot T-M1)
question: At T3, what is established about ingot-n4 (whose mass was measured as mm1 against its accepted alias bar-0417)? Is a mass value of ingot-n4 established, with what status and on which evidence?
justification: facts_about selects contents by the subject's identity class (FA §1; ID-D §3.8). same-as(ingot-n4, bar-0417) is accepted by the system (its own claim) and timeless (ID-3), so bar-0417's contents are ingot-n4's. At T3 the only content involving the class is mm1's has-quality(bar-0417, mass, [2.5, 2.506] kg) attested over [T2, T4); mm2/mm3 start T6 and mo1/mo2 at T10. same-as is an identity type and the measurement activity is an event, so neither is listed (FA §1). The content is established (one accepted assertion, no rival under any constraint; GAP-MEAS-6 means no slot dispute) and its status is the core rule over a basis-observation claim: ASSERTED (CM §3 'observation gives ASSERTED'; v0.2 §5.6 OBSERVED not produced). Evidence: support of an established entry is supporting (FA §6). The identity link relied on is not added to the evidence (HO §4, ID-D §3.10), so sa1 is not admissible; the other measurements do not hold at T3. The measurements reader is not used because the contracts do not say whether it judges the bearer with its same-as group (ambiguities.md A-1).
uncertainty: Status ASSERTED rests on 'observation gives ASSERTED' (CM §3) and OBSERVED not being produced (§0.3).

competency: M4 a corrected measurement: which value is current and which is history (same attester)
question: mm2 (2.512 kg) was corrected by mm3 (2.509 kg). Listing all of ingot-n4's mass measurements (no t), which is current and which is history, and does the superseded one keep its own record?
justification: mm3 is the system's own measurement with supersedes mm2 (same attester). For the system, which accepts its own claims, mm3 is accepted and mm2 superseded (ME §4, core-0.3 supersession); the superseded attestation keeps its own record (stage-c 'Correction'), so its raw value 2.512 is still reported. usable requires not superseded, so mm2 is not usable. M4 gold names current by acceptance=accepted and history by acceptance=superseded (ME §6). mm3's range: [2.509 - 0.004, 2.509 + 0.004] kg (factor 1). Evidence: mm3 is a usable measurement (supporting). Other usable entries the full list may contain are admissible: mo1 (lab-orsa's, accepted by the system, whose correction the system has not accepted) and mm1 (recorded against the alias; whether it is listed is not fixed). mm2 (superseded) and mo2 (unreviewed) are alternatives: forbidden.

competency: M4 a correction the perspective has not accepted: the original stays current for the system
question: lab-orsa measured mo1 (2.530 kg), which the system accepted, and later corrected it with mo2 (2.511 kg), which the system has not reviewed. In the system's perspective at T11, which of the two is current?
justification: ME §4: supersession is per perspective, and a perspective keeps the original until it accepts the correction. The system accepted mo1 and never accepted mo2, so mo1 stays accepted and usable, and mo2 (another attester's claim nobody in the system perspective accepted) is unreviewed. Both hold at T11 ([T10, T12)), as does mm3 (persists from T6 until superseded; system, accepted). mo1's range [2.530 - 0.006, 2.530 + 0.006] kg. Evidence: usable measurements mo1 and mm3 support; mo2 is an alternative; mm2 is superseded.

competency: M4 corrected measurement seen from the correcting attester's perspective
question: In lab-orsa's own perspective, listing ingot-n4's mass measurements (no t), which of mo1 and mo2 is current, and what is the current range?
justification: lab-orsa's perspective is its own attestations plus its acceptances (v0.2 §6.2). Its correction mo2 supersedes its own mo1, so for lab-orsa mo2 is accepted and mo1 superseded (ME §4; supersession per perspective). The superseded attestation keeps its record (raw 2.530). mo2's range [2.511 - 0.006, 2.511 + 0.006] kg. Evidence: mo2 is the only usable measurement for lab-orsa; the system's measurements mm1 to mm3 are unreviewed for lab-orsa (alternatives) and mo1 is superseded.

competency: M6 calibration at measurement time when no certificate names the instrument
question: Was gauge-6 calibrated when it took measurement c6 at T7?
justification: t = T7 selects only c6 (an explicit instantaneous measurement at T7; SD-MEA-1, SD-MEA-2). Its activity names gauge-6, and no certificate names gauge-6. attested is the calibration_status answer at the activity's start (MC §2, §4). CS §3: 'Not established' with no certificates means no calibration is recorded at all; with nothing found the status is NOT_YET_KNOWN (CS §2 status), and support is empty for undecided answers (C-4). certificates lists every certificate naming the instrument: none. The stated reference is reported as exact text (MC §2). Evidence: c6 is usable (supporting, P-MC-1); no calibration claim exists to cite.
uncertainty: reference_check.check is not expected: with no certificate for the instrument, the order between 'no certificate recorded for the instrument' and other checks is not fixed (ambiguities.md A-6).

competency: M6 calibration not yet effective at measurement time
question: Was gauge-1 calibrated when it took measurement c1 at T8, given that certificate cert-g1 (whose reference c1 states) is valid only from T10?
justification: t = T8 selects c1 only (instant at T8; c3's start window begins T9). Calibration is judged at c1's activity start, T8 (MC §4). cal-g1 is accepted (system) and holds over [T10, T25): at T8 it is not yet effective (CS §2 judgement vocabulary; incB holdings labels), and nothing else names gauge-1, so rule Q reaches step 4: not yet effective (CS §3). support is empty for an undecided answer (C-4). The stated reference 'G1-2026' equals cert-g1's reference and cert-g1 names gauge-1: matches a certificate, reported beside the attested judgement and never reconciled (MC §3). Evidence: SD-MEA-5 makes the accepted claim of a not-yet-effective certificate supporting (CS §6 row 'certificates[judgement=not yet effective].evidence[acceptance=accepted]'), so cal-g1 is required with c1 (usable).

competency: M6 calibration in the gap between an expired certificate and a renewal not yet effective
question: Was gauge-7 calibrated when it took c7 at T16, between cert-g7a (valid to T15) and its renewal cert-g7b (valid from T17)?
justification: t = T16 selects c7 only. At c7's start T16: cal-g7a held over [T1, T15) and has ended (expired); cal-g7b starts T17 (not yet effective). CS rule Q order (CS §3): no dispute; no established holding; denied or expired applies (cal-g7a), before 'not yet effective': judgement expired, support the expired holding's support [cal-g7a], status by the core rule over it: ASSERTED. An expired holding is not a conflict (C-3). Each certificate keeps its own judgement in certificates (CS §2). The stated reference 'G7-1' is cert-g7a's: matches a certificate. Evidence: c7 (usable) and cal-g7a (support of an expired judgement, CS §6) are required; cal-g7b is the accepted claim of a not-yet-effective certificate, admissible under SD-MEA-5 though the overall judgement is expired.

competency: M6 calibration claimed only by an unreviewed source
question: Was gauge-5 calibrated when it took c5 at T6, when the only calibration claim for it is calibra-house's, which the system has not reviewed?
justification: t = T6 selects c5 only. cal-g5 is attested by calibra-house and accepted by nobody in the system perspective: unreviewed. CS §3 per-content labels: unreviewed (pending) is not established; with no other holding, the judgement is not established. Something is found (a certificate claim), so the status is UNKNOWN rather than NOT_YET_KNOWN (CS §2), and support is empty for an undecided answer (C-4). Evidence: c5 is usable (supporting); unaccepted certificate claims are alternatives (CS §6, MC §6), so cal-g5 is forbidden.

competency: M6 calibration when the activity start is an uncertain window inside which the certificate's validity ends (slot T-M5)
question: Measurement c3's activity started at some unknown instant in [T9, T13]; gauge-3's certificate cert-g3 was valid only until T11. Was gauge-3 calibrated when c3 was taken?
justification: t = T13h12 selects c3 (it certainly holds then: start <= T13, end T14) and no other measurement. Calibration is judged at the activity's start (MC §4), here the window [T9, T13]. SD-MEA-6: calibration is established only if established throughout the whole possible start window; agreement at the bounds is insufficient, no arbitrary instant is selected, and every internal validity transition counts. cal-g3 holds over [T1, T11): established for starts in [T9, T11), expired for starts in [T11, T13]. It is therefore not established throughout; nor is it expired or denied throughout (SD-CAU-10: certainty only across every admissible case), and there is no dispute. Of CS's judgement labels only 'not established' remains; something was found, so status UNKNOWN; support is empty for an undecided answer (C-4). Evidence: c3 is usable; cal-g3 is the accepted claim whose judgements are kept, admissible but not required (no row of the evidence tables makes it supporting for a 'not established' judgement).
uncertainty: The overall label 'not established' is derived by elimination from the CS judgement vocabulary; SD-MEA-6 itself says only that the answer is not 'established'. The 'at' field and per-certificate judgement over the window are not expected.

competency: M6 calibration disputed at measurement time (accepted calibration beside an accepted denial)
question: Was gauge-4 calibrated when it took c4 at T20, given the system's calibration claim from cert-g4 and qa-dept's denial over [T18, T24), which the system accepted?
justification: t = T20 selects c4 only. At its start T20, cal-g4 (system, accepted, [T1, until superseded)) is an established holding and cal-g4-deny (qa-dept, polarity false, accepted by the system, [T18, T24)) is an accepted denial of the same calibration content. CS rule Q step 1: an established holding beside an accepted denial is disputed; status DISPUTED; support empty for disputed answers (C-4). The calibration judgement never invalidates the measurement (MC §3). The stated reference 'G4-B' is cert-g4's: matches a certificate. Evidence: c4 is usable (supporting); for a disputed attested judgement the accepted assertion and accepted denial are conflicting (CS §6, MC §6, P-CS-1).

competency: SD-MEA-2 explicit instants: two explicit instantaneous measurements at the same instant, compared (slot T-M4)
question: Measurements l1 and l2 of mast-m5's length were both taken at the instant T12 (start, no end). Do they agree within their stated uncertainties?
justification: SD-MEA-2: an explicit instantaneous measurement (measure with a start, no end, not persists) holds at its instant, and two at one instant may be compared subject to the other conditions; the SD-CAU-5 table lists measurements(t=12) of such a measurement as listed. Both hold at T12 and nothing else about (mast-m5, length) does (l16, l17 end T11). Same k (2), identical condition texts, same SI unit: comparable. l1 = 12000 mm +/- 20 mm = [11.98, 12.02] m; l2 = [12.06, 12.14] m; 12.02 < 12.06, so the ranges are disjoint under closed bounds: incompatible, DISPUTED (CM §3). Evidence: both are in an incompatible pair, so conflicting, not supporting (CM §6).

competency: SD-MEA-2 explicit instants: an instantaneous measurement does not hold an hour later
question: Which length values of mast-m5 hold at T12 10:00, one hour after the instantaneous measurements l1 and l2 at T12 09:00?
justification: SD-MEA-2: an explicit instantaneous measurement holds at its instant; instant, empty interval and persistent content stay distinct, so l1 and l2 (T12 09:00, no end, not persists) say nothing about T12 10:00 and are not included (SD-MEA-1 includes only attestations whose verdict at t is not silent). No other length attestation of mast-m5 holds at T12h10 (l16/l17/d1 end by T11; l3 starts T16). The list is empty; nothing is cited.

competency: SD-MEA-1 t as valid time: half-open end of a measurement interval
question: At T18, which length values of mast-m5 hold? Is l3 (taken over [T16, T18)) still listed?
justification: SD-MEA-1: t is valid time and only attestations whose verdict at t is not silent are included. A measure content is attested over the activity's interval (fixture-format measure), and valid-time intervals are half-open (SD-CAU-5), so l3 over [T16, T18) does not hold at T18 and is not listed; l4 over [T17, T19) holds. No other length attestation of mast-m5 holds at T18. l4's range: 12.5 +/- 2 x 0.125 = [12.25, 12.75] m. Evidence: l4 is a usable measurement (supporting); l3 is not part of the answer.

competency: SD-MEA-1 t as valid time: an accepted denial of a measured content covering t is listed (slot T-M3)
question: At T9 12:00, which length attestations about mast-m5 are in force, given that the system accepted its own denial d1 of l16's measured content over [T9, T10)? How are l16 and the denial each listed?
justification: SD-MEA-1: every attestation whose verdict at t is not silent is included, denials too, each with its acceptance and role. At T9h12, l16 [T8, T11), l17 [T9, T11) and the denial d1 [T9, T10) are all in force; all are the system's own, hence accepted. usable requires polarity true (ME §2), so the denial is listed but not usable, and the denial does not change l16's own acceptance or usability: readers report, they do not discard (ME §3 'nothing is combined or reconciled'). l16's range: 12.0 +/- 0.25 = [11.75, 12.25] m. Evidence: usable measurements l16, l17 support (P-ME-1). The ME table makes denials alternatives, while §0.4 lists accepted denials as conflicting; the denial is therefore not required in any role but admissible as conflicting.
uncertainty: The role of an accepted denial in a measurements answer (alternative per the ME table, conflicting per §0.4) is not settled; gold neither requires nor forbids citing it as conflicting (ambiguities.md A-4). d1's kind is not expected.

competency: SD-MEA-4 disjoint valid times: incomparable even with disjoint ranges
question: mast-m6's length was measured at the instant T3 (l9, 12.0 m) and at the instant T4 (l10, 12.4 m). Over all times (no t), do the two measurements disagree?
justification: SD-MEA-4: measurements whose valid times do not overlap are incomparable, since every quantity may change (v0.2 clarification B: 'non-overlapping valid times for a changing quantity'). l9 holds only at T3 and l10 only at T4 (SD-MEA-2), so their pair is incomparable although their ranges [11.98, 12.02] and [12.38, 12.42] are disjoint. No comparable pair is incompatible, so the status is the core rule over the compared (usable, basis observation) measurements: ASSERTED (CM §3). Evidence: CM §6 makes compared measurements outside an incompatible pair supporting, while §0.4 lists incomparable claims as alternatives; gold therefore admits l9 and l10 as supporting without requiring them.
uncertainty: Supporting role of incomparable measurements (CM §6 vs §0.4 'alternative: incomparable'); see ambiguities.md A-5.

competency: SD-MEA-3 categorical values are read through holds, not the measurement readers
question: Is mast-m5's surface finish galvanised at T15? And is it painted at T15?
justification: SD-MEA-3: measurements and compare_measurements cover interval-valued quantities only; categorical values are read through holds / facts_about. holds addresses exact content: type plus the given role bindings (SD-CORE-1). s1: cat1 is the system's own attestation of has-quality(mast-m5, surface-finish, finish-galvanised) from T1 until superseded: accepted, holds at T15, status ASSERTED (core rule), support [cat1] (HO §6). s2: no attestation of the painted content exists; has-quality is not a functional slot (GAP-MEAS-6), so the accepted anodised claim cat2 gives no exclusivity inference and is about a different content; nothing about the content is visible: NOT_YET_KNOWN, holds None (§0.3; HO §2). Evidence: cat1 supports s1; cat2 is not evidence for either content.

competency: M2 agreement where one measured content is denied by an accepted denial (slot T-M2)
question: At T9 12:00, l16 [11.75, 12.25] m and l17 [12.0, 12.5] m overlap, but the system has also accepted its own denial d1 of l16's measured content. Do the measurements agree, and what is the answer's status?
justification: The compared measurements are the usable ones (accepted, polarity true): l16 and l17; the denial d1 is not a measurement and is not compared. Their pair: same k, same condition text, overlapping valid times; ranges overlap under closed bounds (12.0 <= 12.25): possibly compatible (CM §3). CM §3 nevertheless records that v0.2 §5.3 makes an accepted assertion and an accepted denial of one content DISPUTED, and that stage-c names 'a polarity denial' as a rival measurement attestation; the behaviour that lists such a denial as an alternative was adjudicated a semantic defect, and questions expecting the contract's DISPUTED answer are eligible. So the status is DISPUTED. Evidence: l16 and l17 are compared measurements outside any incompatible pair (supporting, CM §6). Accepted denials are conflicting evidence (§0.4), so d1 is required conflicting evidence; l16, as the denied side, is also admissible as conflicting (one attestation may hold different roles in different components, §0.4).
uncertainty: The fixture's deny step must address exactly the content measure l16 writes; its coverage-level parameter is written as erf(2/sqrt 2) because the contracts do not state the coverage-level formula (ambiguities.md A-2).

competency: M2 agreement within uncertainty: ranges touching at one bound (closed-bound overlap)
question: At T17 12:00, l3 gives [11.75, 12.25] m and l4 gives [12.25, 12.75] m. Do the two measurements agree within their stated uncertainties?
justification: Both hold at T17h12 (l3 [T16, T18), l4 [T17, T19)), with k = 2, identical condition texts and the same SI unit: comparable. Overlap uses closed bounds ($la <= $ub; $lb <= $ua; CM §3): 11.75 <= 12.75 and 12.25 <= 12.25, so they overlap at the single value 12.25: possibly compatible, which is not agreement and gives no intersection (v0.2 clarification B). No incompatible pair, so the core rule over basis-observation measurements gives ASSERTED. The bounds are exact in binary floating point (calc sheet). Evidence: both compared, neither in an incompatible pair: supporting (CM §6).

competency: M3 different coverage factors: incomparable, not disputed
question: At T21 12:00, l5 (k = 2) and l6 (k = 3) of mast-m5's length have disjoint ranges. Are they in conflict?
justification: CM §3: incomparable when the coverage levels differ (no harmonisation, v0.2 C4, GAP-MEAS-3). k = 2 and k = 3 give different coverage levels, so the pair is incomparable even though [11.98, 12.02] and [12.27, 12.33] are disjoint (v0.2 §7 C4 variant: k = 3 vs k = 2 is incomparable). No comparable incompatible pair: status by the core rule, ASSERTED. Ranges use each measurement's own k (calc sheet). Evidence: supporting role of incomparable measurements is unsettled (CM §6 vs §0.4), so admissible, not required.
uncertainty: Supporting role of incomparable measurements; see ambiguities.md A-5.

competency: M3 different stated conditions (exact text, differing only in capitalisation)
question: At T25 12:00, l7 was taken under 'wind below 2 m/s' and l8 under 'Wind below 2 m/s'. Their ranges are disjoint. Are they in conflict?
justification: Conditions are kept as exact text (ME §2; D-C-7) and pairs are incomparable when the condition texts differ (CM §3); there is no condition ontology to equate them (GAP-MEAS-2). 'wind below 2 m/s' and 'Wind below 2 m/s' differ as text, so the pair is incomparable despite disjoint ranges ([11.98, 12.02] vs [12.28, 12.32]). Status: no comparable incompatible pair, so ASSERTED. Evidence as M-032.
uncertainty: Supporting role of incomparable measurements; see ambiguities.md A-5.

competency: M3 three measurements: one under different conditions beside an incompatible comparable pair
question: At T28 12:00, l13 and l14 were taken under 'wind below 2 m/s' and l15 under 'wind gusting 8 m/s'. Which pairs are comparable, which conflict, and what is the overall status?
justification: One comparison per pair (CM §5). l13 [11.98, 12.02] and l14 [12.18, 12.22]: same conditions and k, disjoint: incompatible. l15 [12.08, 12.12] has a different condition text, so l13-l15 and l14-l15 are incomparable (CM §3), although l15 is disjoint from both. Any comparable incompatible pair makes the status DISPUTED (CM §3). Evidence: l13 and l14 form the incompatible pair (conflicting, CM §6); l15 is compared but outside any incompatible pair, supporting by CM §6 but an incomparable claim by §0.4, so admissible only.
uncertainty: Supporting role of incomparable measurements; see ambiguities.md A-5.

competency: M1 stated value at an instant: raw value and unit kept, range in SI
question: Which length values of mast-m5 hold at T12, and for l1 (written in millimetres) what raw value, raw unit, standard uncertainty, coverage factor, conditions and SI range were recorded?
justification: The SD-CAU-5 boundary table: an explicit instantaneous measurement at 12, asked at t = 12, is listed (SD-MEA-2); l1 and l2 are the only length attestations of mast-m5 at T12. ME §2: the range is [v - k u, v + k u] in the dimension's SI unit: (12000 -/+ 20) mm x 0.001 = [11.98, 12.02] m; the record keeps the raw value, raw unit, u and k as written and conditions as exact text (D-C-1, D-C-7; v0.2 clarification B 'faithful preservation'). The system's own claim: accepted. Evidence: l1 and l2 are usable measurements (supporting).
